evidence.text: The equity securities book probably took a Q3 mark-to-market LOSS. Marketable equities were $155.5m at 6/30/26, about 32% of $482m equity, and Alphabet was the largest holding (10-Q note 5). The rest is financial-services stocks. GOOGL closed 357.37 on 6/30 and 344.08 on 9/30 (−3.7%), and KBWB went 92.98 to 87.23 (−6.2%). At −4 to −6% on the book, the after-tax loss is about $4.5-7m, or −$2 to −$3 a share. GAAP EPS would then be roughly $2-3, against $11.49 in Q2 2026 and $7.85 in Q3 2025, while core EPS is unaffected. Conditional on a print today the size is −0.3; weighted by about 25% probability of a print in the window it is −0.08.

HIFS has no sell-side model publishing a GAAP number. If the loss were priced, I would expect a visible pre-print discount relative to book. Instead the stock trades at about 1.27x the 6/30 book of $230.83, with no visible discount.

evidence.text: The Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, its first hike since 2023, and projected another this year. CME had priced the hike above 90% beforehand, so short-term rate expectations rose through Q3. Hingham is liability-sensitive: $1.405bn of FHLB advances and $1.915bn of wholesale funds against $2.084bn of retail and commercial deposits. Its NIM expansion was already slowing: +15bp in Q1 to 2.04%, then +10bp in Q2 to 2.14%, with the cost of interest-bearing liabilities falling only 5bp in Q2 against 14bp in Q1. Q3 NIM is likely flat to only slightly up, and Q4 NIM faces a reversal. That would break the narrative of core returns 'improving materially over time'. Conditional on a print the size is −0.6; probability-weighted it is −0.15.

evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no reaction history in the baseline (FDIC filer). Q1 2026's +15bp NIM step and Q2's +10bp step came with a flat core EPS ($4.79, then $4.82), and the stock fell −1.2% after the Q2 print.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The stock is −6.2% over 20 days and KBWB fell 8.5% in September. What is not priced is the company-level number: Hingham does not guide, so its Q3 NIM and cost of funds are seen for the first time in the release. If the stall were priced, HIFS would have lagged the bank index in September, and it did not: HIFS ran 288 (8/31) to 283 (9/30), −2%, against KBWB −8.5%.
evidence.independence: The Q2 2026 release (https://www.hinghamsavings.com/assets/2026/07/PRESS-RELEASE-Q2-2026.pdf) shows the slowing deceleration in the cost of interest-bearing liabilities. The macro-to-company transmission is a proxy that the company has not confirmed.

evidence.text: Q1 FY2027 (quarter to 2026-05-31) showed franchise and royalty fees down 26% year on year ($1.232m vs $1.655m) because of revised franchise agreements with lower royalty and marketing fees. G&A rose 28% ($1.280m vs $1.001m) on the franchise website and delivery-platform rollout, and the net loss widened to $1.168m from $0.324m. Both are structural and carry into Q2. If royalty fees fall about 26% again against Q2 FY2026's $1.640m (about -$0.4m), total revenue lands below the year-ago $6.82m and the loss lands wider than the year-ago $0.66m, unless product sales (+3.5% in Q1 on price, plus the fifth company store from 2026-07-15) make up the difference.
evidence.resolves_by: 2026-10-13 if the print is 2026-10-12 amc (last year's pattern); no later than 2026-10-16 if the release comes by the 2026-10-15 10-Q deadline. This is AFTER the sealed 10-12 bmo window.

The run-up came on the sale-leaseback, which bears on the balance sheet, not the P&L.

evidence.text: On 2026-10-06 RMCF sold its Durango HQ, factory and warehouse for $6.6m (independent appraisal) to American Heritage Legacies, a company controlled by Interim CEO Allen Harper's family. RMCF leases the property back for 10 years at $624k in year one (9.45%) with 2% annual escalators. Interest falls by about $792k a year against $624k of rent, and the 2027 maturity and that lender's security go away. Expect the Q2 10-Q to carry this as a subsequent event, possibly with a gain on sale and revised going-concern or covenant language.
